Kenya, Big Skys and Great Migration

Kenya sits at the heart of East Africa, bordered by Tanzania, Uganda, South Sudan, Ethiopia, and Somalia, with a scenic coastline along the Indian Ocean. As the region's original safari pioneer, Kenya has long been synonymous with the classic African adventure, its capital, Nairobi, is one of the few cities in the world with a national park at its doorstep, offering visitors the surreal experience of viewing lions and giraffes against a backdrop of skyscrapers. Kenya's diverse geography spans the Great Rift Valley, snow-capped Mount Kenya, vast savannah plains, and pristine coral coastline, making it a destination capable of delivering wildlife, culture, adventure, and beach relaxation all within a single itinerary.


From a tourism standpoint, Kenya's global reputation rests heavily on the Maasai Mara National Reserve, the northern stage of the Great Migration and one of the most famous wildlife-viewing destinations on Earth, alongside a strong network of well-established parks, luxury lodges, and tourism infrastructure built up over more than a century of safari tourism. The country is also home to vibrant, deeply rooted cultures, most notably the Maasai, whose traditions have become intertwined with Kenya's tourism identity through community-based tourism experiences. With Nairobi serving as a major regional aviation hub, well-developed roads connecting key parks, and a long-standing hospitality sector catering to both budget and luxury travelers, Kenya remains one of Africa's most accessible and internationally recognized tourism destinations.
